handoff.summary: Cycle 2: completed T-003 (protocol skeleton) and T-004 (determinism + rewind) in src/domain. forkChoice.ts (LMD latest votes with order-independent equivocation tie-break, GHOST descent, smallest-index ties), finality.ts (SLOTS_PER_EPOCH=4, checkpointFor with empty-boundary fallback, supermajority=ceil(2n/3), justification fixpoint, adjacent-epoch 1-finality), protocol.ts (round-robin proposer, buildProposal, buildAttestation), simulation.ts (SimulationConfig{validatorCount,seed}, advanceSlot: propose→all attest→recompute finality/heads, stateAtSlot = pure recomputation = rewind). All shared-view/instant delivery for now. typecheck/test/build exit 0 (16 files, 128 tests). phase1-core remaining: T-005 only.
next_actions: Run T-005 (local views): introduce a message-visibility model (which validator has seen which block/vote as of which slot) so each validator gets its own View {validator, slot, blockTree, votes} and per-validator finality/heads genuinely diverge under future interventions. Refactor advanceSlot to compute per-validator views instead of the shared tree+votes, keeping stateAtSlot recomputation and all existing tests green (adjust the shared-head test to derive heads from per-validator views).

Design note for T-005: keep delivery instant-by-default (visibility = everything) so current behavior is the identity case; partitions/delays (T-009) then become visibility filters at slot boundaries, not engine changes.
After T-005, phase2 (T-006 UI shell) begins: replace the M1 UI; delete src/core, src/protocol, src/ui and their tests when the new UI lands, and rewrite README.md for the new design then.

Semantic choices recorded (discretion, not semantics changes of the reference types): SLOTS_PER_EPOCH=4; checkpoint epoch derived from block slot; same-slot equivocation resolved lexicographically for fork choice; anchor at slot 0, first proposal at slot 1.
Counters: completed_todos_since_reset=4 (reset threshold 5) — expect a context reset after the next completed Todo; write the handoff accordingly.
